criteria.criterion: AC1: Memory governance cleanup is scheduled to run daily at 03:00 UTC
AC2: GovernanceService.runCleanup() executes all four sub-jobs and returns GovernanceResult
AC3: expireMemories() sets status='rejected' for all memories where ttlAt < now() and returns count
AC4: downrankStaleLowConfidence() sets confidence=0.1 for memories older than 90 days with confidence < 0.3
AC5: deduplicate() finds all (projectId, kind, subject, predicate) combos with more than one active memory, keeps highest confidence, marks others as superseded
AC6: applySupersession() finds DECISION memories on same topic ordered by createdAt DESC, keeps newest active, marks older ones as superseded
AC7: Governance jobs are idempotent - running twice produces same end state
AC8: Governance run touching 1000 memories completes in under 30 seconds
AC9: Governance jobs never delete MemoryItem rows - only update status, confidence, or supersededBy to preserve audit history

reasoning: Implementation is clean, correct, and follows all project conventions. The MemoryGovernanceService properly implements all four cleanup sub-jobs (expireMemories, downrankStaleLowConfidence, deduplicate, applySupersession) with pagination for large datasets. The MemoryGovernanceProcessor correctly schedules daily cleanup at 03:00 UTC and iterates across all projects. No DELETE operations are used - all mutations go through upsert() to preserve audit history. Idempotency is achieved by checking activeKey before applying changes. Performance is addressed with 100-item pagination batches. All 1003 tests pass across 49 suites.
